neetpg2025-q001: The jugular foramen transmits the glossopharyngeal (IX), vagus (X) and accessory (XI) nerves, the inferior petrosal sinus, the sigmoid sinus continuing as the internal jugular vein, and meningeal branches. The hypoglossal nerve passes through the hypoglossal canal.
neetpg2025-q002: A patent ductus arteriosus (or the ligamentum arteriosum structure) derives from the left sixth aortic arch. The defect shown is related to the left 6th arch, while the right 4th arch becomes the proximal right subclavian artery.
neetpg2025-q004: The muscles of facial expression are supplied by the facial nerve, and the muscles of mastication (e.g. masseter, temporalis, pterygoids) are supplied by the mandibular division of the trigeminal nerve. The key matches the labelled muscles to the mandibular and facial nerves.
neetpg2025-q005: Meralgia paraesthetica is entrapment of the lateral cutaneous nerve of the thigh (L2, L3) as it passes under or through the inguinal ligament near the anterior superior iliac spine, causing numbness over the anterolateral thigh.
neetpg2025-q006: A forceful eversion injury of the ankle stretches or tears the deltoid (medial) ligament, which is strong and often avulses the medial malleolus. Inversion injuries damage the lateral ligaments, mainly the anterior talofibular ligament.
neetpg2025-q007: The long head of the triceps arises from the infraglenoid tubercle of the scapula. The long head of the biceps arises from the supraglenoid tubercle.
neetpg2025-q008: Transitional epithelium (urothelium) lines the ureter, bladder and part of the urethra. It has dome-shaped (umbrella) surface cells and can stretch as the organ distends.
neetpg2025-q010: Thiazides increase calcium reabsorption in the distal convoluted tubule, reducing urinary calcium excretion. This lowers the risk of calcium stone formation in hypercalciuria.
neetpg2025-q012: Kearns-Sayre syndrome (ophthalmoplegia, retinitis pigmentosa, cardiac conduction defects) is a mitochondrial DNA disorder inherited only through the mother. Williams syndrome, achondroplasia and cystic fibrosis are nuclear gene disorders.
neetpg2025-q013: At altitude, hypoxia stimulates the peripheral chemoreceptors, causing hyperventilation and washout of CO2. The primary disorder is respiratory alkalosis, with renal compensation by bicarbonate excretion.
neetpg2025-q015: Bleeding gums, petechiae, perifollicular haemorrhages and bone fractures in a child indicate scurvy (vitamin C deficiency). Vitamin C is a cofactor for prolyl (and lysyl) hydroxylase in collagen synthesis.
neetpg2025-q016: Jaundice with bleeding that corrects with a vitamin K injection suggests cholestasis (biliary obstruction), where bile salts are lacking and fat-soluble vitamin K is poorly absorbed. In liver parenchymal disease vitamin K does not correct the coagulopathy.
neetpg2025-q017: After 3-5 days of fasting, the brain uses ketone bodies (acetoacetate and beta-hydroxybutyrate) as its main fuel. This spares muscle protein because less glucose is needed from gluconeogenesis.
neetpg2025-q018: High phenylalanine with a normal phenylalanine hydroxylase suggests deficient tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4), the cofactor, or its recycling enzyme dihydropteridine reductase. This is atypical (malignant) PKU, and the diet alone doesn't prevent neurological damage.
neetpg2025-q019: In vitamin B12 deficiency, homocysteine cannot be converted to methionine by methionine synthase, so homocysteine and methylmalonic acid rise. The fall in methionine is the downstream effect.
neetpg2025-q020: Hexosaminidase A deficiency causes Tay-Sachs disease, in which GM2 ganglioside accumulates in neurons, producing a cherry-red spot, hyperacusis and neurodegeneration.
neetpg2025-q021: Long-term diuretic use can lead to thiamine deficiency, causing wet beriberi (heart failure with peripheral neuropathy). The key marks thiamine, as urinary loss of thiamine is increased by loop diuretics.
neetpg2025-q022: Inserting one nucleotide near the start of the mRNA (the 4th position of 900) shifts the reading frame for all codons downstream, so a completely different amino acid sequence results, usually with a premature stop codon.
neetpg2025-q023: Skin cancers and photosensitive hyperpigmentation point to xeroderma pigmentosum, a defect in nucleotide excision repair that normally removes UV-induced pyrimidine dimers.
neetpg2025-q024: Tall stature with long limbs, arachnodactyly, hypermobile joints, high-arched palate, lens subluxation (upwards) and aortic regurgitation is Marfan syndrome, caused by a mutation in the fibrillin-1 (FBN1) gene.
neetpg2025-q025: Orange tonsils with very low HDL (5 mg/dL) and normal triglycerides is characteristic of Tangier disease (ABCA1 mutation), with cholesterol ester deposition in the tonsils. The key lists familial hypercholesterolaemia, which is doubtful.
neetpg2025-q026: High LDL cholesterol with normal triglycerides and tendon or subcutaneous xanthomas, in a family with similar disease, is type IIa hyperlipoproteinaemia (familial hypercholesterolaemia). Type IIb also has raised triglycerides.
neetpg2025-q027: Caspases are activated in apoptosis (caspases 3, 8, 9) and in pyroptosis (caspase 1, 4, 5, 11 via the inflammasome). Necrosis is caspase independent.
neetpg2025-q028: A 68-year-old with bleeding and a peripheral smear showing promyelocytes with Auer rods (faggot cells) has acute promyelocytic leukaemia, with t(15;17) (PML-RARA), responsive to ATRA.
neetpg2025-q030: A well-circumscribed, homogeneous, non-haemorrhagic painless testicular mass in a young man is a seminoma, the commonest germ cell tumour. It is very radiosensitive, with fried-egg cells and lymphocytes on histology.
neetpg2025-q031: A suprasellar mass in a child with wet keratin and calcification is an adamantinomatous craniopharyngioma, derived from Rathke's pouch remnants. It causes visual disturbance and growth failure.
neetpg2025-q032: Jaundice and splenomegaly in a teenager with a family history and high MCHC (spherocytes) suggest hereditary spherocytosis, an autosomal dominant disorder of ankyrin, spectrin or band 3.
neetpg2025-q033: Flow cytometry uses fluorescent-labelled antibodies to identify and quantify CD markers on individual cells, for immunophenotyping leukaemia and lymphoma.
neetpg2025-q034: A neck mass with calcitonin-producing tumour cells expressing synaptophysin and chromogranin (neuroendocrine markers) is medullary thyroid carcinoma, derived from parafollicular C cells. It is associated with MEN 2 and RET mutations.
neetpg2025-q035: Transitional epithelium with umbrella cells lines the urinary bladder and ureter.
neetpg2025-q036: Inheritance only through the mother and passed to all offspring of an affected woman is mitochondrial inheritance, as in Kearns-Sayre syndrome and Leber hereditary optic neuropathy.
neetpg2025-q037: Dry eyes and dry mouth with anti-Ro (SSA) and anti-La (SSB) antibodies is Sjogren syndrome, in which CD4 T-cell lymphocytic infiltration destroys the lacrimal and salivary glands.
neetpg2025-q038: Benralizumab is a monoclonal antibody against the interleukin-5 receptor alpha. It depletes eosinophils and is used in severe eosinophilic asthma.
neetpg2025-q039: In a migraine patient with coronary artery disease, triptans and ergotamine are contraindicated because of vasoconstriction. Propranolol is the safe prophylactic option and also treats hypertension.
neetpg2025-q040: Pegloticase is a recombinant PEGylated uricase that oxidises uric acid to allantoin, which is more soluble and easily excreted. Rasburicase works similarly.
neetpg2025-q041: Metoclopramide, a D2 antagonist and 5-HT4 agonist, raises the lower oesophageal sphincter tone and speeds gastric emptying. Proton pump inhibitors reduce acid, and alginate forms a physical barrier.
neetpg2025-q042: Thiazide diuretics decrease urinary calcium excretion, but they can cause hypercalcaemia and other metabolic effects. The question key marks decreased calcium excretion as the cause of stones; thiazides in fact reduce calcium stones.
neetpg2025-q043: In HIV patients with tuberculosis, antitubercular therapy is started first, and antiretroviral therapy is started within 2 to 8 weeks (earlier, within 2 weeks, if CD4 below 50). The key marks ATT first then ART after 2 weeks.
neetpg2025-q044: The BPaLM regimen (bedaquiline, pretomanid, linezolid and moxifloxacin) for 6 months is the recommended regimen for MDR/RR-TB, including in HIV patients. Monitor for drug interactions and immune reconstitution syndrome.
neetpg2025-q046: For prophylaxis of recurrent PSVT, oral verapamil, diltiazem or beta blockers are used. IV adenosine is used for the acute termination of PSVT.
neetpg2025-q047: Persistent nocturnal asthma on short-acting bronchodilators needs a controller: inhaled corticosteroids with a long-acting beta agonist (LABA). Salbutamol is for relief only.
neetpg2025-q048: Lipoteichoic acid on group A streptococcus helps in adherence to pharyngeal epithelial cells, along with M protein and fibronectin-binding proteins.
neetpg2025-q050: Dysentery after drinking raw milk with Gram-negative curved (comma or seagull-shaped) rods is caused by Campylobacter jejuni, a common cause of bacterial diarrhoea and the antecedent of Guillain-Barre syndrome.
neetpg2025-q051: Nocturnal perianal itching in a child with eggs on a cellophane (Scotch) tape test is enterobiasis (pinworm), caused by Enterobius vermicularis. Treatment is albendazole to the whole family.
neetpg2025-q052: Small intracellular yeasts with narrow-based budding in a patient with chronic cough and weight loss (looks like TB) is histoplasmosis, caused by Histoplasma capsulatum. It is a dimorphic fungus found in bat and bird droppings.
neetpg2025-q053: Gram-positive, branching filamentous bacteria that are acid-fast on a modified ZN stain and grow on paraffin-baited media are Nocardia asteroides, which causes pneumonia and brain abscess/meningitis in the immunocompromised.
neetpg2025-q054: Septate hyphae with acute-angle dichotomous branching in BAL fluid, in a patient with fever, cough and haemoptysis, is aspergillosis. Mucor has broad aseptate hyphae with right-angle branching.
neetpg2025-q055: Painful vesicular lesions in the mouth with multinucleated giant cells and intranuclear inclusions on the Tzanck smear are the findings of herpes simplex virus infection (gingivostomatitis).
neetpg2025-q056: Recurrent infections with Neisseria (gonorrhoeae or meningitidis) suggest a deficiency of the terminal complement components (C5 to C9), which form the membrane attack complex. The terminal complement assay (CH50) evaluates it.
neetpg2025-q057: A necrotic skin lesion (malignant pustule) in a farmer with capsulated Gram-positive bacilli in chains seen by polychrome methylene blue (McFadyean reaction) is cutaneous anthrax, caused by Bacillus anthracis.
neetpg2025-q058: A middle-aged man from an endemic area with progressive swelling of the lower limb and microfilariae on the peripheral smear has lymphatic filariasis, where the swelling is from lymphatic obstruction (lymphoedema).
neetpg2025-q059: Severe abdominal pain, throat irritation, vomiting of blood and bile, and diarrhoea after ingestion is acute arsenic poisoning (garlic breath, rice-water stools). Phosphorus poisoning has a luminous vomit and garlic odour.
neetpg2025-q060: Under Indian law a girl below 18 years cannot give valid consent to sexual intercourse, so her consent is irrelevant (statutory rape under IPC 375 and POCSO). The boy is liable regardless of her statement.
neetpg2025-q061: Curved scratch marks (fingernail) on one side of the neck and grouped bruises (finger tips) on the other, with no ligature mark, indicate manual strangulation (throttling).
neetpg2025-q062: The Zasko phenomenon is a post-mortem tendon reflex, elicited when the tendon is struck soon after death. It reflects the persistence of the muscle's excitability.
neetpg2025-q063: A person who commits a crime and claims insanity at the time of the act should first be sent for psychiatric evaluation to judge whether he knew the nature of the act (M'Naghten rule / Section 84 IPC), as the court decides on the report.
neetpg2025-q064: The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012, covers all children below 18 years of age, both boys and girls. It makes the offences gender neutral.
neetpg2025-q065: A death report from a hospital that is sent without active case-finding is passive surveillance, where reporting depends on the reporting unit, and no one goes out to look for cases.
neetpg2025-q066: In the de facto method of census, people are counted at the place where they are found at the time of enumeration, whereas the de jure method counts them at their usual place of residence.
neetpg2025-q067: The Nalgonda technique for defluoridation of water uses alum (aluminium sulphate) and lime (for pH), then bleaching powder for disinfection, with flocculation and sedimentation.
neetpg2025-q068: The steps in a randomised controlled trial are: selection of the population, randomisation into study and control groups, manipulation (intervention), follow-up, and assessment of outcome.
neetpg2025-q069: Outward bending of the lower limbs and osteoporosis in a young adult in Andhra Pradesh (a fluorosis belt), with a rice and jowar diet, is skeletal fluorosis. Prevention is defluoridation of water, so the key's 'fluoride supplementation' looks wrong.
neetpg2025-q070: Under the National Urban Health Mission, one urban primary health centre serves 50,000 population (in slum areas, and a UPHC per 50,000 in non-slum areas). The key is 42.
neetpg2025-q071: To compare the mean of a quantitative variable (haemoglobin) between two independent groups, the unpaired (independent samples) t-test is used. The paired t-test is for before and after values in the same persons.
neetpg2025-q072: Anopheles larvae lack a respiratory siphon and lie parallel to the water surface, breathing through spiracles. Culex and Aedes larvae have a siphon and hang at an angle.
neetpg2025-q073: A child with bowing of legs from rickets (vitamin D deficiency) due to poor sun exposure is addressed by the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) scheme, which provides supplementary nutrition and health services for children under 6.
neetpg2025-q074: Under the Weekly Iron and Folic Acid Supplementation (WIFS) programme, adolescents aged 10-19 years receive one tablet each week containing 100 mg elemental iron and 500 micrograms of folic acid. The key marks 60 mg iron with 500 micrograms, which is the dose for younger children.
neetpg2025-q075: Under the population strategy for coronary artery disease prevention, dietary cholesterol should not exceed 100 mg per 1000 kcal per day.
neetpg2025-q076: Evaluation measures the extent to which objectives and targets of a health programme have been achieved, and assesses the quality of the results. Monitoring is the continuous checking of activities.
neetpg2025-q077: Allocating whole health centres (clusters) randomly to the intervention or control arm is a cluster-randomised controlled trial.
neetpg2025-q078: Generation time is the interval between acquisition of infection and maximum infectivity of the host. The serial interval is the gap between primary and secondary cases.
neetpg2025-q079: Better 5-year survival with no change in mortality, because screening detects the disease earlier, is lead-time bias. Survival appears longer only because the diagnosis was made earlier.
neetpg2025-q080: A mass causing nasal obstruction and recurrent epistaxis in a young boy is classically a juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma, a vascular tumour of adolescent males. It arises near the sphenopalatine foramen.
neetpg2025-q081: A large, advanced squamous cell carcinoma of the larynx in an elderly patient with a long history of hoarseness and dysphagia is treated by total laryngectomy (or chemoradiation). Partial laryngectomy is for early lesions.
neetpg2025-q082: Recurrent ear infections with a sudden popping sensation, and an otoscopic finding of a tympanic membrane perforation, causes conductive hearing loss in the same ear (left conductive loss).
neetpg2025-q083: Walsham's forceps are used for reduction of a fractured nasal bone (manipulating the nasal pyramid), while Asch's forceps correct the septum. Luc's forceps are for nasal polyp removal and Tilley's forceps for foreign body and nasal packing.
neetpg2025-q084: A well-defined tumour in the cerebellopontine angle in a middle-aged woman with progressive unilateral hearing loss, tinnitus and unsteadiness is a vestibular schwannoma (acoustic neuroma), which widens the internal auditory canal.
neetpg2025-q085: A central tympanic perforation with chronic discharge and hearing loss is mucosal (tubotympanic) chronic suppurative otitis media, safe type. After the ear is dry, the treatment is myringoplasty (or tympanoplasty). Mastoidectomy is for the unsafe (squamosal) type with cholesteatoma.
neetpg2025-q086: Recurrent anterior septal bleeding that fails packing and chemical cautery from Little's area is treated by ligation of the anterior ethmoidal artery (for bleeding from above the middle turbinate), and the sphenopalatine artery for posterior bleeding. The key marks anterior ethmoidal.
neetpg2025-q087: White, dandruff-like deposits on the anterior lens capsule are the classic sign of pseudoexfoliation syndrome, associated with glaucoma, zonular weakness and complications in cataract surgery.
neetpg2025-q088: Intacs are intrastromal corneal ring segments inserted into the cornea to flatten and regularise its shape, treating keratoconus (and post-LASIK ectasia).
neetpg2025-q089: A slowly growing painless mass lateral to the lateral canthus for years in a young person is typically an external angular dermoid cyst, a choristoma that lies at the frontozygomatic suture.
neetpg2025-q090: Guttae (excrescences on Descemet's membrane) in one eye and bullous keratopathy in the other indicate Fuchs endothelial dystrophy, a bilateral corneal dystrophy in which endothelial pump failure causes corneal oedema.
neetpg2025-q092: Orbital cellulitis is infection posterior to the orbital septum, with proptosis, painful limited eye movement and chemosis. Ethmoid sinusitis is the commonest source, especially in children, and it needs IV antibiotics rather than topical ones.
neetpg2025-q093: A tall boy with long limbs and bilateral ectopia lentis (upward displacement) has Marfan syndrome, caused by mutations in the fibrillin-1 (FBN1) gene on chromosome 15.
neetpg2025-q094: Alpha-L-iduronidase deficiency is Hurler syndrome (MPS I). The undegraded glycosaminoglycans that accumulate are dermatan sulfate and heparan sulfate.
neetpg2025-q095: Adenosine deaminase deficiency causes accumulation of toxic metabolites in lymphocytes and gives severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID), with recurrent infections and failure to thrive in infancy.
neetpg2025-q096: For a baby born to an HIV-positive mother with a detectable viral load (high risk), dual prophylaxis with nevirapine and zidovudine is given for 6 weeks. Low-risk infants receive nevirapine alone.
neetpg2025-q097: A child with chronic kidney disease and bow legs has renal osteodystrophy (CKD-mineral bone disorder). Treatment aims to correct calcium and phosphate balance, so calcium supplementation is given according to the key, with active vitamin D and a phosphate binder where required.
neetpg2025-q098: A child with a febrile convulsion who is still seizing in the emergency room is given a benzodiazepine first, i.e. diazepam (rectal or IV) or lorazepam or midazolam.
neetpg2025-q099: A neonate with severe respiratory distress and bowel loops seen in the chest on X-ray, with a mediastinal shift and a scaphoid abdomen, has a congenital diaphragmatic hernia (usually left sided through the foramen of Bochdalek).
neetpg2025-q100: A child with neurodegeneration, a cherry-red spot and hexosaminidase A deficiency has Tay-Sachs disease, a GM2 gangliosidosis.
neetpg2025-q101: Progressive external ophthalmoplegia, pigmentary retinopathy and cardiac conduction block with a pedigree showing only maternal transmission is Kearns-Sayre syndrome, a mitochondrial DNA deletion disorder.
neetpg2025-q102: Vials suitable for vaccines are those of the correct type for cold chain storage. As per the key, vials 1 and 2 shown in the image can be used for administering vaccines.
neetpg2025-q103: Between days 21 and 25 of a 28-day cycle (the late luteal phase), the corpus luteum is regressing, so progesterone is high and oestrogen is relatively low, with LH low. Hormone levels fall just before menstruation.
neetpg2025-q104: The Brandt-Andrews manoeuvre (controlled cord traction with counterpressure above the pubic symphysis) is used in the active management of the third stage of labour, to deliver the placenta safely and avoid uterine inversion.
neetpg2025-q105: For cord prolapse in active labour, the presenting part is manually elevated to relieve pressure on the cord, and the mother is put in knee-chest or Trendelenburg position, followed by an urgent caesarean section.
neetpg2025-q106: Irregular heavy bleeding at 46 years with a thickened endometrium on ultrasound needs endometrial biopsy to exclude hyperplasia or carcinoma, because of the risk in perimenopausal women.
neetpg2025-q107: In the Pritchard regimen the loading dose is 4 g IV (20% solution) plus 10 g intramuscular (5 g in each buttock), i.e. a total of 14 g. The maintenance dose is 5 g IM every 4 hours.
neetpg2025-q108: Atonic PPH not responding to medical therapy (oxytocin, ergometrine, carboprost, misoprostol) is managed by uterine tamponade, such as a Bakri balloon, before surgical options like compression sutures.
neetpg2025-q109: Painless postmenopausal bleeding is endometrial carcinoma until proven otherwise. Endometrial thickness and biopsy are investigated.
neetpg2025-q110: A woman in a trial of labour after a previous caesarean who develops fetal distress or signs of scar rupture requires an emergency caesarean section. Uterine rupture is the major concern.
neetpg2025-q111: The sequence of manoeuvres for shoulder dystocia is: McRoberts and suprapubic pressure first, then Rubin (internal rotation), then delivery of the posterior arm or the Gaskin all-fours position, and Zavanelli as a last resort.
neetpg2025-q112: In the repair of an episiotomy, the vaginal mucosa is closed first, then the muscle and fascia, and finally the skin.
neetpg2025-q113: MRI showing a thickened junctional zone (above 12 mm) with myometrial cysts in a woman with chronic pelvic pain and dysmenorrhoea is adenomyosis.
neetpg2025-q114: A postmenopausal woman with vaginal bleeding needs a pelvic examination and investigation for endometrial malignancy (ultrasound, Pap smear, endometrial sampling), as hypertension raises the risk. Blood pressure control is secondary.
neetpg2025-q115: Secondary amenorrhoea with raised FSH (36 IU/L) and a very low AMH at age 36 indicates premature ovarian insufficiency (ovarian failure before 40 years).
neetpg2025-q116: Crown-rump length measured in the first trimester (6-13 weeks) is the most accurate ultrasound parameter for dating a pregnancy, accurate to within 5-7 days.
neetpg2025-q117: A prolactinoma (high prolactin) suppresses pulsatile GnRH secretion from the hypothalamus, reducing LH and FSH. This causes amenorrhoea and infertility.
neetpg2025-q118: Cervical cancer with hydronephrosis or a non-functioning kidney due to tumour invasion is FIGO stage IIIB, regardless of other findings. IIIA is lower vaginal involvement and IIIC is lymph node metastasis.
neetpg2025-q119: In a breech delivery, if the arms are extended or winged, the Lovset manoeuvre is used to deliver them, by rotating the body through 180 degrees to bring each arm in front. Mauriceau-Smellie-Veit delivers the after-coming head.
neetpg2025-q120: Breast tenderness, linea nigra and a bluish cervix (Chadwick's sign) are probable signs of pregnancy. Confirmatory signs include fetal heart sounds, fetal parts and ultrasound.
neetpg2025-q121: A woman with a BMI over 35, a caesarean section and pre-eclampsia is at high risk of thromboembolism, so low molecular weight heparin prophylaxis is advised after delivery.
neetpg2025-q122: A normal umbilical cord has two arteries (carrying deoxygenated blood to the placenta) and one vein (carrying oxygenated blood to the fetus).
neetpg2025-q123: Circumferential full-thickness burns of the limb produce a tight eschar that can compromise circulation, so an escharotomy is the immediate step to relieve pressure.
neetpg2025-q124: In Parks classification, an intersphincteric fistula tracks between the internal and external sphincters and is the commonest type (about 70%). Trans-sphincteric tracks through the external sphincter.
neetpg2025-q125: The knot shown, with an additional twist (double throw) on the first throw, is a surgeon's knot, which holds better under tension.
neetpg2025-q126: Breast cancer with skin involvement and inflammation (peau d'orange, redness over one third of the breast) is T4d, inflammatory carcinoma. T4b is skin ulceration or satellite nodules, and T4a is chest wall extension.
neetpg2025-q127: Varicose veins with skin changes such as pigmentation, lipodermatosclerosis and eczema (CEAP C4) show chronic venous insufficiency, and a venous ulcer can develop.
neetpg2025-q128: Polypropylene (Prolene) is a non-absorbable monofilament suture. Silk and nylon braided are multifilament. Catgut is derived from collagen.
neetpg2025-q129: A 3-year-old with ballooning of the prepuce on micturition and a narrow, non-retractile foreskin has phimosis. True (pathological) phimosis is due to scarring, whereas physiological phimosis is normal in young children.
neetpg2025-q130: A pulsatile neck mass that does not fill on carotid compression but refills when released and a splaying of the carotid bifurcation (lyre sign) on angiography suggests a carotid body tumour (chemodectoma).
neetpg2025-q131: A well-defined, extra-axial, dural-based mass with homogeneous enhancement and a dural tail on MRI is a meningioma, the commonest benign intracranial tumour.
neetpg2025-q132: Initially conscious, then becoming unconscious after a road accident, with multiple small petechial haemorrhages in the white matter and corpus callosum at autopsy, indicates diffuse axonal injury caused by rotational acceleration-deceleration forces.
neetpg2025-q133: The investigation shown is cystoscopy, a direct visualisation of the bladder through a scope inserted via the urethra. It is an invasive procedure and is the gold standard for bladder tumours (with biopsy).
neetpg2025-q134: Manometry is the confirmatory investigation for achalasia cardia (failure of LES relaxation and absent peristalsis), after a barium swallow shows a bird-beak appearance.
neetpg2025-q135: A homogeneous opacity in the right upper zone with an elevated horizontal fissure and shift of the trachea to the right is right upper lobe collapse.
neetpg2025-q136: MRI of the sacroiliac joints is the earliest modality to show sacroiliitis (bone marrow oedema) in ankylosing spondylitis, before any changes show on X-rays, which appear after years.
neetpg2025-q137: Sudden generalised muscle rigidity, rapid rise in temperature and tachycardia under general anaesthesia is malignant hyperthermia, treated with IV dantrolene, which blocks the ryanodine receptor.
neetpg2025-q138: Atracurium (and mivacurium) cause histamine release leading to flushing, rash and hypotension. Cisatracurium has little histamine release.
neetpg2025-q139: An emergency surgical cricothyroidotomy gives a temporary airway when the upper airway is obstructed. It must be followed by a formal tracheostomy within 24-48 hours. It is not for prolonged use.
neetpg2025-q140: A lateral lumbar spine X-ray showing forward slip of one vertebra over another with a defect in the pars interarticularis (Scottie dog collar) is spondylolisthesis.
neetpg2025-q141: Rhomboid-shaped, positively birefringent crystals in the synovial fluid are calcium pyrophosphate crystals, diagnostic of pseudogout (CPPD disease). Gout has needle-shaped negatively birefringent urate crystals.
neetpg2025-q142: A young man with inflammatory back pain, morning stiffness that improves with exercise and anterior uveitis has axial spondyloarthritis. MRI of the sacroiliac joints is the most sensitive test for early disease.
neetpg2025-q143: Bone pain, an increasing hat size, warm bones and a raised alkaline phosphatase with normal calcium is Paget disease of bone, with a mosaic pattern of increased bone turnover.
neetpg2025-q144: Severe pain out of proportion after a tibial shaft fracture, with tense swollen leg, is acute compartment syndrome. It needs immediate fasciotomy to prevent ischaemic muscle necrosis.
neetpg2025-q145: Flashbacks and amnesia for a traumatic event within the first 2 weeks to 1 month is acute stress disorder (ASD). If symptoms last longer than a month, it becomes PTSD.
neetpg2025-q146: A person found at a place with no memory of the journey, and confusion about their identity or travel, has dissociative fugue (now a specifier of dissociative amnesia), where there is purposeful travel.
neetpg2025-q147: A rigid preoccupation with punctuality, order, perfectionism and control is the pattern of obsessive-compulsive personality disorder (anankastic personality). Unlike OCD, there are no true obsessions or compulsions.
neetpg2025-q148: Receiving a special meaning from a perception, in the form 'follow the birds because God is giving orders', is a primary delusion, as in delusional perception. It can't be explained by the perception itself.
neetpg2025-q149: A patient who commits a crime and claims mental illness must be sent for psychiatric evaluation to determine fitness to stand trial and criminal responsibility (Section 84 IPC), before any judgement.
neetpg2025-q150: Found in another town with no memory of how he got there after a traumatic event such as an earthquake is dissociative fugue, which usually follows severe stress.
neetpg2025-q151: Involuntary perioral movements after long-term antipsychotics are tardive dyskinesia. Management is to stop or switch the antipsychotic (clozapine) and give a VMAT2 inhibitor such as tetrabenazine, valbenazine or deutetrabenazine.
neetpg2025-q152: An itchy rash on the elbows and buttocks with gluten sensitive enteropathy and granular IgA deposits in the dermal papillae is dermatitis herpetiformis. Treatment is dapsone and a gluten-free diet.
neetpg2025-q153: A non-progressive, hypopigmented patch since birth or childhood with a mildly white accentuation under Wood's lamp and diascopy that is negative (no blanching) is nevus depigmentosus. In vitiligo, the patch is chalky white and progressive.
neetpg2025-q154: An indurated plaque with central atrophy on the face, in a patient with apical lung calcification (old tuberculosis), is lupus vulgaris. PCR for Mycobacterium tuberculosis is the most appropriate test, as the biopsy shows few bacilli.
neetpg2025-q155: Irregular swelling of the foot with multiple discharging sinuses and black granules is eumycetoma (Madurella). A KOH mount of the black grains shows dark, septate, slender dematiaceous hyphae.
neetpg2025-q156: Squamous cell carcinoma of the base of the tongue (oropharynx) is now most often caused by human papillomavirus infection (HPV-16), with a better prognosis than tobacco-related cancers.
